prerequisites: Secondary school knowledge of mathematics and physics
Fundamentals of vector, differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be informed about the fundamental laws and theories of classical and modern physics and trained to apply this knowledge to simple physical systems, to explain and predict the behaviour of such systems.
Students will be exposed to physics as the theoretical basis and fundament of engineering disciplines.
Knowledge of the fundaments of classical and modern physics on the university level in the field of classical mechanics, oscillations and waves, gravitational field and thermodynamics.
Comprehension of general physical principles and capability to apply them to specific physical systems.
Ability to carry out physical calculations by means of application of vector, differential and integral calculus.

syllabus_topics: The international system of units, changing units
Motion in two and three dimensions, velocity and acceleration, uniform circular motion
Newton’s first, second and third laws
Work done by general variable force
Potential energy and conservation of energy
Determining gravitational and elastic potential energy values
Work done by external and nonconservative forces
Newton’s second law for a system of particles
Newton’s second law in angular form
Tension and compression, shearing, hydraulic stress
Simple harmonic motion, the force law, energy
The principle of superposition for waves
The zeroth law of thermodynamics and temperature
The internal energy and the first law of thermodynamics, applications
The second law of thermodynamics and entropy
Heat engines, refrigerators and heat pumps
Efficiency of a heat engine: Stirling engine
Numerical solution of equation of motion: Torque oscillations
Numerical and graphical solution: Heat transfer

assessment_methods.method: Continuous check in the form of tests in the seminars

assessment_rules: Final classification reflects the result of continuous check in the form of tests in the seminars. The final examination consists of the obligatory written test and facultative oral part. Attendance at seminars and labs is checked by the teacher. Absence may be compensated for by agreement with the teacher.
